My very fondest memory of dwarf fortress was one of my first fortresse's. I'd watched a bunch of tutorials on youtube, I was using the noob pack. I thought I was prepared. Ho boy was I wrong

The embark started out easily enough, I has followed the suggestions of the tutorials and picked an easy starting area to cut my teeth on plenty of minerals, no aquifer, no evil, you know the drill. As you do I had a little bit of a slow start trying to get the hang of the key commands, no biggie everything seemed to be going smoothly. I got a little burrow dug out, was growing plump helmets as my main source of food, was brewing beer from them, I even built a nice little cafeteria and put a couple of tables in it.

My fortress began to grow quickly, I think i kind of bungled up the trading, but it didn't really matter since it was an easy embark. Before I knew what had happened I had a roaring fortress with over 300 citizens to my name (334 If I do recall). Little did I know that I had quietly sown the seeds of my own destruction, 327 dwarves would die for my mistake.

Everything seemed to be going in swimmingly. But slowely season by season, a strange lethargy seemed to spread through my fortress. Productivity began to steadily decrease, for no reason that I could diacern. Dwarves were actually starving to death even though my larders were full. Eventually I did find the source of the problem, but by the time I had it was far too late to avert the Fun that all my dwarves were about to have. You see, dwarves are nothing if not a bunch of tempramental fucks, who will gladly eat their lunch on the ground, but as soon as there is a single table in the fortress they will pig headidly (at least in the patch I was using) insist on eating their meal at that table. And I had two, two table for 334 hungry dwarves. My dwarves literally started to starve to death, with food in their hands, waiting in line to use one of the two tables.

I realized my mistake at just about the time the fun started, I received the notification that a dwarf had starved to death and I paused the game to see where. He was about two spots in line away from a table. Upon the starvation of this dwarf all hell broke loose. In a Tantrum spiral I have come to call the cafeteria riots 300 dwarves flew into all blind rage. One of the first things to happens is that an angry dwarf smashed one of the tables, from there all hope was lost. (If he had smashed both maybe the others would have sat down and eaten what they were holding on the ground)

When all was said and done only 7 dwarves remained, one adult and six children, infants really. A couple of whom I believe had been birthed in the cafeteria during the riots. The lone adult declared himself mayor and called a town meeting in one of the plump helmet fields for some reason, when none of the children showed up he went mad. 327 dwarves died, I e driven to madness, and 6 children presumably left to die from neglect, because I hadn't ordered enough tables.

And that's the story of why I never put less than 50 tables in my fortress caffeteria's to this day.
